reason: Driven in chromium at 1440x960, ?v=light&state=full, and every number the seat gives is exact. Tab 1-3 are the tab strip, 4-6 the three anchor KPI cards, and Tab 7 is the first .dot. On that press .scroll moves from 0 to 4 of 664 available; the mark's box is [948,960] in a 960px viewport; getComputedStyle(.dot).scrollMarginBottom is 0px and .scroll has scroll-padding auto. The focus ring (outline 2px, outline-offset 3px) therefore ends at 965.2 and its entire bottom stroke is off-screen. .strip-scale sits at [963,980] and the .ages card's own bottom edge at 1005 - the scale reading 'today / 15d / 30d / 45d' and 45px of the card are below the fold. All nine marks then hold at [948,960] for the whole traversal: scrollTop never moves off 4 again, so the axis calibration is absent for every one of the nine keyboard stops, and the card reads as a card someone forgot to finish. The screenshot at the moment of focus shows a 12px dot pinned to the window edge under an open-bottomed ring with a bare hairline under it. The mechanism is narrower and more interesting than the seat says, which is why it survived: Blink scrolls sequential focus with kAlignCenterIfNeeded, so a mark that is wholly out of view gets centred and a mark that is PARTIALLY visible gets the bare minimum. At 1280x900, 768x1024, 390x844, and in quiet/partial/first-run at 1440, the strip starts fully below the fold and the first mark lands centred at 444/766/416/474 with the scale and the card's bottom edge all in view. Only 1440x960 in the full state puts the first mark 4.2px past the fold at rest - and 1440x960 full is the frame this surface is shot and graded at. Nothing in the 366-assertion behaviour gate touches focus-scroll landing (its .dot work is scrollIntoViewIfNeeded() plumbing at 420/428/1014/1190, not where focus parks the mark), so this is not a restatement of anything proven. It is also the named class 'Focus that leaves the screen - keep the focused element scrolled into view through every move' from the paid-for library, creeping back in its partial form: the element is in view, its indicator and its meaning are not. Severity 'defect' is the right class and I would not move it. Not misleading - nothing on the surface asserts something untrue; not blocking - each mark's aria-label and its visible tooltip both carry 'open N days', the tooltip still places above the mark with room (tip [896,940] against a dot top of 948), and the fortnight rule with its 'A FORTNIGHT' label is still on screen at 888-905, so relative position remains legible. The seat's 'no way to tell 2 days from 41 days except by reading nine tooltips one at a time' overstates the rhetoric a little; the corrected consequence - the calibrated scale, the card's bottom edge and the bottom of the focus ring are all unavailable to the one reader who must move through the strip mark by mark - is still a defect at the declared bar. The proposed fix is correct and its numbers are right: 48px is the rung that works, not a guess. With scroll-margin-bottom: var(--gap-hall) the box the browser must satisfy becomes [948,1012], still partially visible, so the minimal scroll is 52px - the mark lands at [900,912], the scale at [915,932], and the .ages card's bottom edge at 957 of 960, i.e. the whole card clears the fold with a hair to spare. var(--gap-room) at 24px would have scrolled only 28px and left the card's bottom edge at 981, still clipped. Verified visually. No constraint is touched: no colour, no weight, no architecture, two existing rungs on the declared ladder, two declarations.
sharpenedFix: Ship it as written - `.dot { scroll-margin-bottom: var(--gap-hall); scroll-margin-top: var(--gap-room); }` - with one honest note on the second value: it is inert at the graded frame. At 1440x960 full, .scroll exhausts at scrollMax 664 before a mark can ever be pinned to the top edge, so scroll-margin-top never fires there; it only shifts the centred landing by 12px at 390/768/1280 and in the shorter states. Keep it anyway - it is the symmetric guard for the taller scroll ranges (390 has 1820px of travel) and it costs nothing - but the bottom value is the one doing the work, and 48 is load-bearing: 24 does not clear the card.
